result.answer: First establish whether any written termination was sent or received and when, and preserve the deadline position; obtain the seven documents listed as missing on the evaluated checklist before assessing form, service, deadlines, or the arrears basis.
open_points: Whether a written termination notice exists, was received, and on what date; the written notice and proof of receipt are listed as missing on the checklist.
The lease contract and notice-period evidence are listed as missing, so the agreed terms and any termination dates cannot be checked.
The stated termination reason, cure notice with termination warning, and rent ledger/payment evidence are listed as missing; the arrears position and payment history cannot yet be verified.
Whether the flat is a family home, whether there is a retaliation concern based on asserted tenant rights, and whether an extension is relevant remain unresolved.
Landlord correspondence is listed as missing but optional. It could also help clarify the landlord’s position.

reply.subject: Your question about the reported termination of your tenancy

clauses.text: We understand that your claim concerns a lease termination reportedly connected with rent arrears.

As a first step, please tell us whether you have since found or received a written termination notice, when it was delivered or collected, and whether you have any registered-mail notification or delivery information. Please send the notice and any available proof of receipt; these are needed to establish the deadline position.
Please also send your lease contract and any documents showing the agreed notice period and termination dates.

Because the termination was reportedly connected with rent arrears, please send any payment-deadline letter or other notice warning of termination, together with a rent account statement and evidence of payments, including the partial payment.

Please also let us know whether the flat is your family home, whether you had asserted any tenant rights before the termination was raised, and whether you may need an extension of the tenancy. Any correspondence with your landlord could also help clarify the position.

learning.title: Clarify uncertain written service in a lease-termination claim
learning.why: When a tenant cannot tell whether a written termination exists or reached them, explicitly ask about delivery indicators (such as a collection notice or tracking information) as well as the notice itself, so the handler can establish receipt and preserve the deadline position.
learning.question: For a lease-termination claim where receipt is unresolved, has the tenant checked for any registered-mail collection notice or delivery record, and can they provide it along with the termination notice if found?
learning.applies_when_text: Apply in a lease-termination dispute when it remains unclear whether a written termination was received.
learning.reason: The customer described a shared-mailbox problem and uncertainty about both a possible notice and registered-mail notification, making explicit inquiry about delivery indicators useful to clarify receipt.
